Even Cover Flow -- a physically impossible floating cascade of albums -- feels instantly familiar, showing familiarity is something users construct from hints rather than perceive, and syncing, playlists, and the Music Quiz game endlessly re-manufacture it (the iPod as the new McDonald's golden arches abroad). Flipping the relation via Actor-Network Theory, he notes the iPod tracks play counts, pushes 'Listeners Also Bought,' and trains our flicking gestures, so that perhaps the iPod becomes familiar with us; the Microsoft Zune figures as the abject, zombie-like copy whose perverse familiarity reveals a politics of recognition, and the closing game of imagining Wittgenstein's playlist endorses natural language's many language games over exact definitions.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Tuomas Manninen asks how Gaiman's recycled mythological figures can be the same characters as their originals when Revelation's male, sword-wielding War becomes Good Omens' arms-dealing Carmine 'Red' Zuigiber and Pestilence retires in 1936 for Pollution, with the problem of talking truthfully about non-existent entities reaching back to Plato's Sophist. David Lewis's 'Truth in Fiction' makes the original author the arbiter of a character's properties, and Amie Thomasson's artifact theory makes fictional characters abstract artifacts created by authors, but only adding the type/token distinction and Wittgenstein's family resemblances, the same criss-crossing network of overlapping similarities by which we count games, lets Revelation's Four Horsemen and Gaiman's Four Bikers be tokens of one type. He closes with Russell's defense of philosophy's value: like Richard Mayhew's tale of London Below, a philosophical answer need not convince or be final to teach us 'what things may be.'

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: . . Blurring the Boundaries
samples.relation: Duncan examines the Sherlockian Game — the century-old practice, founded in Ronald Knox's 1911 parody 'Studies in the Literature of Sherlock Holmes,' of treating Holmes and Watson as real people — through Wittgenstein's account of 'game' in Philosophical Investigations: no common feature defines games, only family resemblances, so the playful-seeming Game legitimately spans idle fun and serious scholarship. Huizinga's 'magic circle' supposedly walls games off from the world, but the Game has blurred that boundary from the start, as fans reconcile why Watson's wife calls him 'James,' hunt the real King of Bohemia, and see their labors honored in Ritchie's bull-pup and Sherlock's James Phillimore. The epistemological payoff is that knowledge and meaning do not reside in the text alone: Game-players playfully shape what they uncover, donning Canonical names like Duncan's own 'Silver Blaze,' so media fandom becomes a way of making knowledge.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 1. Reading the Signs
samples.relation: Di Bernardo reads the religious language of The Walking Dead as sustained irony - a 'doubleness of sense' - arguing that the walkers, churches, and signs comment critically on faith rather than endorse it. He tracks the church scenes (the Southern Baptist church of 2.1 'What Lies Ahead' with its timed bells and sitting-dead congregation, Gabriel's Saint Sarah's where Maggie answers that it is 'just four walls and a roof'), the ambiguous 'sanctuary' and Terminus signs, and the comic-book Jesus (Paul Monroe) as a machine-gun savior, concluding that the scriptural promise of eternal life through consuming flesh and blood yields only undead life. Against Epicurus's consolation that death is nothing to us, and in the shadow of Nietzsche's madman announcing the death of God, the chapter warns against investing absolute trust in any signs - religious or secular - a warning capped by Rick biting out Joe's throat as his own 'day of reckoning.'

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Irwin takes Pilate's Quid est veritas as a guided tour of theories of truth applied to the film: Gibson's sympathetic Pilate embodies relativism, met with Nietzsche's 'truth is a woman' perspectivism and Baudrillard's postmodern laughter and rejected; Caiaphas and the bad thief demanding Jesus come down from the cross put the correspondence theory to work ('the proof is out there'), though beliefs hang on other beliefs ad infinitum; Simon of Cyrene's growing conviction models the coherence theory, exposed as necessary but not sufficient by Swinburne's case for versus Wells's case against the divinity of Jesus; and Pilate's Barabbas gambit parodies James's pragmatic theory, where working is not enough if there is no corresponding reality. He then retrieves Heidegger's reading of aletheia as uncovering, helped by the Quid est veritas anagram ('Est qui vir adest': it is the man before you) and Gadamer on truth seizing us like beauty, so that Jesus's 'I am the truth' and Claudia's dream-guided warnings point to truth as disclosure. Since disclosure alone cannot decide between inconsistent revealed claims, Irwin ends by leaving the viewer with a leap of faith and a first instinct as final answer.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: Does the Totem Tumble
samples.relation: Randall Auxier claims to settle whether the totem tumbles: it does, but it does not matter, because the top was Mal's totem rather than Cobb's — Cobb spins it as mourning for the wife whose trust he destroyed by handling her totem, while Cobb's real totem is the gun, which Saito must use (shooting them both in Limbo) once Cobb finally takes the leap of faith and entrusts his life to another person. Building on Bergson's memory theory — the past 'gnaws into the future,' all dreaming is remembering, and shared dreaming is possible because embodied species-memory can be tapped with the right chemist — the chapter recasts Cobb's rule against building from memory as the need to introduce gaps between dream and world, and his inability to keep architecting as personal memory increasingly overrunning perception with age. Through Whitehead's process philosophy — narrative as algebraic order, space as 'frozen time,' generic contrasts like 'and then I ate it' — he also defends the film's 'selective physics': at each level the same five minutes disperses across a larger dreamspace, diluting the gravitational carryover while geometrically expanding dream time.

samples.book: 025 - The Beatles and Philosophy - Nothing You Can Think that Can't Be Thunk
samples.title: CHAPTER 4 “A REVELATION TO BEHOLD”
samples.relation: Argues that the Beatles' devotion to rock and roll was a literal religious phenomenon rather than loose metaphor: Lennon's first hearing of Elvis is analyzed as a William James-style conversion, the Radio Luxembourg broadcasts were treated 'like scripture,' Hamburg was a 'baptism by fire,' and Epstein's new suits at the Cavern were announced as 'a revelation.' Drawing on James's Varieties of Religious Experience and Pragmatism, the chapter reads Beatlemania's screaming crowds as collective ecstatic ritual and the 'toppermost of the poppermost' chant as the will-to-believe making its own truth, in the way James says truth 'happens' to an idea. Aristotle's four causes supply the metaphysical frame — the 'magic' of Liverpool and the sacred quality fans reported are formal-final causation against the material-efficient causation of disenchanted modernity — while the band's double irony ('tarrying with the negative,' after Hegel) let them hold skepticism inside belief, as in Lennon's 'flaming pie' origin parody and the 'more popular than Jesus' episode.

samples.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
samples.title: Reason to Believe When There’s None
samples.relation: Couch takes a night drive through Springsteen's road songs guided by Karl Jaspers's 'ultimate situations' — death ('Wreck on the Highway,' the bottomless gorge under the cruise-controlled life), suffering (the never-ending badlands, shared in Tom Joad's ghost), struggle (violent like 'Johnny 99,' loving as the search for 'one clear moment of love and truth'), and guilt ('Everybody's got a secret, Sonny'; 'you learn to sleep at night with the price you pay'). Jaspers's Existenz-philosophy — built on Kierkegaard's inward self and Nietzsche's diagnosis of the herd, against Kant's optimism about knowledge — explains the songs' endless border-crossings as attempts to evade limits that cannot be evaded, and the fear that turns 'your God filled soul' to 'devils and dust.' The answer to how there's a 'Reason to Believe' is Jaspers's leap of philosophic (not religious) faith toward the unknowable Transcendent, chosen in complete freedom.

samples.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
samples.title: 2. Dystopia from a Woman’s Point of View
samples.relation: Robison-Greene reads The Handmaid's Tale as Atwood's answer to Nineteen Eighty-Four—a dystopia 'from the female point of view'—comparing how both regimes suppress critical thought by banning women's reading, rewriting texts (the Marx slogan 'from each according to her ability' passed off as St. Paul), and manufacturing perpetual war. She deploys Nietzsche's 'monumental' abuse of history, Kierkegaard's leap of faith (Offred's three contradictory versions of Luke's fate), and doublethink to show that believing contradictions becomes both the regime's tool and the victim's survival strategy. The woman's lens adds that reducing women to reproductive function (Marthas, Aunts, Jezebels) thrives where thinking is suppressed, that Beauvoir's point about women's complicity in their oppression is embodied by the Aunts, and that Offred and Nick's affair, like Winston and Julia's, is the act of freedom the Party can never quite own.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Brett Chandler Patterson reads Lost through C. S. Lewis's Chronicles of Narnia as myth rather than allegory - the Lamp Post station and flight 316 (the Prince Caspian dedication page) wink at the source - with the island, like Narnia, a world of crisis and second chances entered by plane crash instead of wardrobe. Flashbacks of past failures (Kate the fugitive, Sayid the torturer, Charlie's addiction, Locke's kidney con) set up struggles for faith that he illuminates with H. Richard Niebuhr on faith as a center of value and revelation as communal, and with Levinas's claim that we become ourselves only through responsibility to the Other in community. The Jack-versus-Locke man-of-science/man-of-faith debate, Charlie's moth-cocoon trial, and Jacob and the Man in Black's black-and-white stone game map onto Aslan versus the White Witch, ending in redemption through the new community and Jack's sacrificial death.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 12. Why Blood Sacrifice
samples.relation: Philip Wilson defines sacrifice as gift-giving with payback ('I give x in order to get y') and reads Thanos's murder of Gamora through Agamemnon's sacrifice of Iphigenia at Aulis, while Black Widow's willing leap from the same cliff parallels Christ's atoning self-sacrifice. The core is Kierkegaard's Fear and Trembling: Abraham's binding of Isaac as the 'teleological suspension of the ethical,' where obeying God suspends universal morality, sharpened by Kant's argument that Abraham should have told the supposed divine voice he could never be certain it came from God. Wilson argues the films restore rather than suspend ethics, Gamora was murdered rather than sacrificed, Natasha died willingly with no collateral harm, and Tony's final 'I am Iron Man' self-sacrifice completes the tragic arc, leaving readers with Kierkegaard's sleepless questions about a moral order that demands blood.

samples.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
samples.title: Does the Totem Tumble
samples.relation: Auxier brings Bergson's memory theory, the past gnawing into the present, all dreaming as remembering, and Whitehead's process philosophy to Nolan's 'pathologies of temporal experience', defending the film's supposedly selective physics: with each deeper level the same five minutes disperses across a larger dream space, diluting the carry-over of effects while time expands geometrically, because 'space is frozen time'. He then re-reads the ending through the narrative gaps the audience was lured across: the top was Mal's totem, which Cobb spin as an act of mourning after handling it and betraying her, and Cobb's real totem is his gun, which Saito uses to shoot them both out of Limbo. The top's tumbling in the finale matters only as a sign that Cobb, the coward who once needed total control over Mal, has finally learned the leap of faith of trusting another person.

name: Moral Psychology (character, vice, weakness of will)

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Abigail Mann argues that the Games only look like 'survival of the fittest': Darwinian natural selection runs on chance ('one slip in thousands') and explicitly rejects the social-Darwinist use of 'unfit' against the poor, while Darwin's Descent of Man explains the tributes' kindness through kin and group selection and an evolved moral sense, so Katniss's unhesitating volunteering for Prim is kin selection and Thresh's conflicted sparing of her shows conscience overriding self-preservation. She tests this against Kant, for whom only duty-motivated action is truly moral, which would make Thresh's inner struggle the more moral act and Katniss's instinctive sacrifice mere animal impulse, and against the egoism of Hobbes (giving to a beggar to relieve one's own distress) and Dawkins's selfish gene, answering with Hume and psychologist Daniel Batson that genuine altruism is real. Her coda: Katniss ultimately rejects Gale not only because his firebomb killed Prim but because it was engineered to trap and kill altruists, and her closing habit of listing 'every act of goodness' is the trilogy's verdict that simple kindness is not an illusion.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: The Doors Are Never Locked
samples.relation: Held reads Cash's Walk the Line retort "Well, they're not Christians then" as a thesis about redemption: since, with Augustine, we rejoice most at the sinner saved, and since the Sermon on the Mount forbids judging what we cannot know (anyone's deep character), humility demands withholding condemnation and hoping even the worst can change. He contrasts Christian redemption, a revaluation of the person that needs outside grace (Cash needed June and the Carters; nobody is self-made), with Nietzsche's attack on redemption as slave-morality self-hatred, granting that Nietzsche's eternal recurrence also revalues the past but objecting that self-revaluation collapses into rationalization, as Cash's Saul in Man in White shows. Forgiveness proper requires repentance and a solvent character, like paying off a debt; the shame of the "Long Black Veil" woman shows why; and because we see "through a glass darkly," nobody, not the Reno murderer, not Joe Bean, is beyond hope, which is why the doors are never locked and why execution or life without parole claims a judgment of moral worth that is not ours to make.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: This Is Really Happening (So Do Something)
samples.relation: Milsky argues that Radiohead practice what environmental virtue ethics preaches, organizing the chapter around Aristotle's akrasia (Nicomachean Ethics VII): Sting, who champions rainforests while advertising Jaguar and topping the 'dirtiest band' carbon table, acts against his own better judgment, whereas Radiohead — confronted with an audit showing their 2003 and 2006 tours emitted roughly 11,368 tons of CO2, mostly from fans driving — changed their actual practice (venues near public transit, car-pool lots, sea freight instead of air, LED lighting and auxilary power units). He reads the King Canute imagery of The Eraser and lines from 'The Clock' and 'And It Rained All Night' as environmental narrative in the tradition of Thoreau's Walden and Leopold's Sand County Almanac, obligating listeners to act or risk akrasia themselves, and presents the band's Friends of the Earth 'Big Ask' commitment as linking environmental virtue to human flourishing. 'Idioteque'''s 'this is really happening' becomes the wake-up call to the akratic fan driving to Lollapalooza with a bottled water.

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: Becoming Good at Being Good
samples.relation: Argues that Zuko's cry 'Why am I so bad at being good?' after burning Toph shows that changing one's explicit self-conception (Korsgaard's practical identity, the description under which you value yourself) does not by itself change one's being-in-the-world (Heidegger): Zuko's perception, dispositions, and rage-fueled firebending still run on the residual identity of the banished prince seeking his father's approval. The chapter traces this friction through the series: releasing Appa triggers a metamorphosis fever, but he still sides with Azula at the Crossroads of Destiny; the regained 'honor' of Book Three leaves him empty ('I should be happy now, but I'm not'); and only after renouncing Ozai, apologizing to Toph, and re-learning fire from the Sun Warriors without rage do his conscious commitments and existential engagement begin to align, culminating in taking Azula's lightning for Katara. Aspiration, in Agnes Callard's sense, is thus a deep change in how one sees and feels, requiring retraining of bodily skills and practical perception, not just new stated values.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: You Don’t Have to Be Like Him to Like Him
samples.relation: Levitt reads Monk through Aristotle's virtue ethics: a man of character whose police virtues survive Trudy's murder but whose phobias produce akrasia — in the pilot he knows he must descend the germ-filled sewer to save Sharona and freezes anyway, doing the right thing only at agonizing cost. Virtue as habit and the golden mean (friendliness as the mean between obsequiousness and standoffishness) frame his slow progress toward acting rightly without thinking, which is also why Stottlemeyer cannot recommend his reinstatement — he doubts the illness, not the man. Aristotle's three friendships sort Monk's relationships: utility (the department, employer Sharona), pleasure, and virtue — Natalie, who after watching Monk save Julie's fish over the priceless moon rock saw her late husband's goodness in him. Ethos, pathos, logos and catharsis then explain viewer identification: watching Monk move from akrasia toward balance (Dr. Kroger's 'N. Hope' note that turns out to mean New Hope) lets audiences identify with, and be ennobled by, a character we would never want to be.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Three 'Phase Four' essays. Moseley reads the Joker across Batman #1, The Killing Joke, The Dark Knight, A Death in the Family, and Dark Knight Returns as a 'moral monster' who knowingly does evil - and, following Anscombe and Scanlon's guise-of-the-good analysis, pursues aesthetic 'higher values' in a Camus-like affirmation of the absurd, embracing the irrationality Batman's rational moral order cannot fathom. Levin uses X-gene biology (Beast's explanation in Astonishing X-Men, genotype vs phenotype, M-Day) to strip Magneto's Homo sapiens superior claim of any genetic or phenotypic basis, then argues via the moral community of rational persons (Kant's criterion) that mutants and humans share one moral community, condemning both the Registration Act and mutant separatism. O'Neil's prose piece traces Harvey Dent from Calvinist certainty through the acid that scars him to cosmic doubt - quantum randomness, many worlds, Sartre's condemnation to freedom - until Nietzsche's amor fati lets him embrace duality and let the scarred two-headed coin decide good and evil.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: Vigilante Hero
samples.relation: Epright and Worth argue that rule-following - the Ten Commandments, the Golden Rule, Kant's categorical imperative (whose consistent Kantian never lies even to Nazis), or the Bentham-Mill principle of utility (whose consistent utilitarian must torture if stakes are high) - never made anyone moral, and Dexter's Code is the case in point: it gives the appearance of morality while licensing murder, and its source (Harry, 'God', the texts) cannot vindicate it. Drawing on Jonah Lehrer's neuroscience that moral judgment is emotional first with reason as post-hoc lawyer, they argue the emotionless Dexter is the madman who has lost everything except his reason, and Kohlberg's moral-development stages find him stuck at the pre-conventional level, below a fifth-grader - punishment-avoidance and you-scratch-my-back reasoning, never universal principles or respect for persons. Real Dexter-inspired killers (Mark Twitchell, Andrew Conley) clinch the verdict: he is neither vigilante hero nor moral agent, just a selfish addict whose rule-governed kills justify nothing.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 9. What Fuckin’ Chance Does a Kid Have
samples.relation: Joseph Westfall argues that Louis's parent-hating bits - the baby he doesn't know who 'might fuckin' hate Jews,' the four-year-old 'asshole,' 'I love her, but I wish she was never born' - voice the real ambivalence of parenthood while showing that children are developmentally incapable of responsibility, so parents must not blame kids for being kids. He contrasts Louis's unknowable, selfish infant with Augustine's doctrine that unbaptized babies are simply evil, and reads Louis's parenting maxim - 'you're not raising the kid in front of you, you're raising the grownup they're going to be' - through childhood as a state of becoming: Jizzanthapuss is on the road to Hitler thanks to his weak mother, and Louie berating little Jane realizes 'I'm her first asshole,' shaping the men she will later attract. Good parenting is keeping kids alive plus forming the future adult, which is why Louis denies his daughters cell phones (they prevent learning empathy face-to-face) and puts his daughter on the smelly city bus while his Mercedes waits.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Obviously, the Borg Can’t Hold Their Liquor”
samples.relation: Decker asks 'What's it like to be a Borg?' and tests whether monist metaphysics justify the Collective: Parmenides's changeless, perfect Being matches the Borg's 'bringing them closer to perfection', Spinoza's one substance (God or Nature) makes assimilationist determinism intelligible and finds truth in Seven of Nine's nostalgia for collective harmony, and Hegel's teleological Geist — the whole 'the world, aware of itself' — most closely mirrors the Borg's galactic quest for an Omega-molecule perfection of 'infinite parts functioning as one.' Yet 'I, Borg' shows Hegelian Spirit working through individuals: Hugh's redemption transforms the Enterprise crew's self-understanding, proving nothing is wholly alien and freedom can coexist with collectivity. Via Haraway's cyborgs and against Kass's 'wisdom of repugnance', the chapter concludes the Borg horrify us because the natural/artificial dualism is already obsolete in our technologized lives — 'if we are the Borg, then resistance truly is futile.'

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 7. Because Nothing Can’t Be!
samples.relation: Joseph Kirkland takes Louis's 'Why? Why? Why?' routine from One Night Stand - collapsing into 'things that are not can't be!' and 'giant ants with top hats dancing around' - as an accidental encounter with the Pre-Socratics' question of why there is something rather than nothing. Louis, he argues, rejects the Principle of Plenitude (a finite world has no room for every possibility), whereas Parmenides argues from pure logic that nothingness is impossible and change therefore illusory - his student Zeno 'proving' it with paradoxes such as the infinite halfway points between Louis and Ben's Pizzeria. Framing the bit with Plato's claim that wonder is the beginning of philosophy and Socrates' unexamined life, the chapter ends on the parental punchline 'bread first, then ethics': feeding the kid trumps metaphysics, and Louis's frustration comes from failing that duty while his daughter probes being and non-being over her French fries.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Meet You on the Dark Side of the Moon
samples.relation: Jere Surber frames Pink Floyd as musical heirs to Parmenides's 'path of Non-Being', then maps Marx's four alienations onto the catalog: self-alienation in 'Brain Damage' ('There's someone in my head, but it's not me'), alienation by things in 'Welcome to the Machine', alienation from other persons in 'Us and Them' and The Final Cut's war trauma, and alienation from species-being in Animals ('Dogs'). Existential absence follows: Sartre's café scene, where the whole ensemble arranges itself around the missing Pierre, parallels the absent Syd and the father killed in World War II behind The Wall ('Comfortably Numb': 'the child is grown, the dream is gone'), while Heidegger's withdrawal of Being accounts for the cosmic Angst of 'Eclipse' and Obscured by Clouds. A postmodern coda reads the band's mid-thought-breaking lyrics and Ummagumma sound experiments as Derridean différance woven through language and sound.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: Yes, but What About the Killer Rabbit
samples.relation: Argues the Pythons invert Arthurian legend's traditional patriarchal function, using Holy Grail — made amid 1970s women's liberation and legal abortion — to expose the absurdity of patriarchy rather than endorse it. The Black Knight's 'None shall pass' embodies an abstract, relationship-blind masculine ethics that the chapter sets against care ethics, while the witch-weighing scene shows Arthur and Bedevere's male bonding eclipsing the mob's victim. Castle Anthrax's 'perilous bed' and the Prince Herbert rescue — Launcelot's heterosexual-matrix heroics collapsing when the damsel in the tower is a prince who enjoys musicals — turn courtly love and gender roles into farce, making the film as much a document of 1970s gender politics as a medieval satire.

samples.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
samples.title: 3. The Flux of It All
samples.relation: Ammon asks whether anything persists beneath Bowie's serial personas, staging Parmenides's denial of change (with Zeno's paradoxes) and Descartes's melting wax against the Heraclitean flux of 'ch-ch-ch-changes.' Rejecting soul-substance views, he takes the empiricist line - Hume's introspection finds only particular perceptions, never a self - warns via the intentional fallacy (Manson's 'Helter Skelter,' Bloom's hawk) against letting Bowie's own pronouncements fix his songs' meanings, and tests 'meaning is use' on Bowie's calling rock stars fascists. Recurring undercurrents (dancing, apocalypse, distrust of authority) survive, but the conclusion is that Bowie's essence just is flux, 'the river we can't step into twice.'

samples.book: 001 - Seinfeld and Philosophy - A Book about Everything and Nothing
samples.title: Was it a Show about Nothing
samples.relation: Eric Bronson takes George's NBC pitch for 'a show about nothing' as a live philosophical problem: Parmenides argued we cannot meaningfully speak of what-is-not (so Art Vandelay is unsayable), but Plato's Sophist answers that nothing is 'otherness' with real power - the puffy shirt is something other than beautiful, and 'The Parking Garage' is doing something other than what is interesting or useful. Lao Tzu's Tao Te Ching goes further: the nameless Tao begets the ten thousand things, and wei wu wei (action through non-action) conquers, as in 'The Chinese Restaurant', where a whole episode of standing in line doing nothing is itself something happening.

samples.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
samples.title: Who is Who
samples.relation: The time-travel chapter grounds Doctor Who's paradoxes in Parmenides and Zeno on the impossibility of change and Aristotle on the logical necessity of past and future statements ('You can't rewrite history!' in 'The Aztecs'), then deploys determinism, David Lewis on the paradoxes of time travel, and the consistency/autonomy principles ('Father's Day,' the Reapers). It uses Leibniz's possible worlds and the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics to read 'Inferno' and 'Turn Left,' arguing quantum indeterminacy and entanglement make the Doctor's 'wibbly-wobbly, timey-wimey' theory of fixed points and flux coherent.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: The Kick—Back to ‘Reality’
samples.relation: Richardson and McWilliams read Inception as an 'existential heist film' by diving through four layers of meaning. At the layer of reality they use Descartes's dream skepticism and wax argument, Hume on belief as custom and cause-effect, and Goffman on being shocked between frames to argue the film makes touch — the fall that wakes, pain ('pain is in the mind'), Saito's wrong-textured polyester carpet, the broken totems (Cobb's top, Arthur's loaded die, Ariadne's holed chess piece) — the only semi-trustworthy sense, while Mal, who locks her totem in the dollhouse safe and picks the dream, replays the cave prisoner who chooses the shadows. The car-chase layer ('downwards is the only way forwards'), Saito's 'old man filled with regrets' limbo, and the pharmacy dreamers who 'come to be woken up' are read through existentialism (Beckett's Waiting for Godot, Jaspers on loneliness and nothingness) and Peirce on the continuity of consciousness, with Cobb cast as the ideological existentialist who chooses action and reality where Cypher in The Matrix and Vanilla Sky's David face the same choice. The chapter then treats the film's reflexivity — the team as screenwriter/producer/director, the Escher-esque Penrose stairs, cross-cut dream time à la Peckinpah — as a lesson in film theory, and finally reaches phenomenology: Cobb's angry projection of Mal shows the dream world displaying his subjective meanings, against Arthur's calm, orderly hotel mindscape.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase One' essays. Dyer reads Mark Millar's Wanted through Plato's cave: Wesley Gibson escapes a pathetic life like the freed prisoner, but like Adolf Eichmann (via Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem) he murders his conscience, so the Fraternity's consequence-free world leaves him numb and unable to value anything - a descent deeper into the cave, ending in the banality of evil. Novy explains why henchmen betray using Aristotle's utility/pleasure/complete friendship distinction (Big Cheese, Henchmen Muenster and Feta): supervillain gangs are Hobbesian pirate crews with no enforcer, so a modus vivendi of self-interest collapses under interrogation and only Machiavellian fear secures loyalty. Foresman applies Goodman and Rawls's reflective equilibrium as a 'cheat' to rank Apocalypse, Magneto, Luthor, the Joker, and Bizarro, concluding the 'best of the worst' is judged on evil ends (or evil means, as with Magneto) and even on glorious failure. Arinder and Milton, in a staged descent-into-madness frame, diagnose mad science in Victor Frankenstein and Dr. Doom as science that denies value-laden theory choice - impossible because data underdetermine theory - breeding the hubris that dehumanizes the scientist.

samples.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This composite chapter argues philosophy through several comics. Jeremy Barris pairs Plato's dialogues with Amazing Spider-Man, using the allegory of the cave, the Forms, and Platonic love/eros to show that Spider-Man's bodily beauty, awkwardness, and self-trivializing irony draw readers toward goodness the way Plato says lust for beautiful bodies leads the soul upward to truth. Iain Thomson reads Moore and Gibbons's Watchmen as a 'deconstruction of the hero,' running Rorschach, Ozymandias and Dr. Manhattan through Nietzsche's Ubermensch and 'do not throw away the hero in your soul,' Heidegger's authentic 'choosing one's hero' and the uncanny, Kierkegaard's knight of faith, and Baudrillard's idea that an extreme realization destroys its own idea. Laura and Paul Canis read Daniel Clowes's Ghost World through Sartre's existentialism: Enid's post-high-school 'three o'clock' limbo enacts thrownness, abandonment, radical freedom and the flight from it into bad faith, contrasting Enid's authentic self-creation with Rebecca's settled conformity. Aldo Regalado's essay treats Tarzan, Superman, Captain America and the Black Panther as responses to modernity and race.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Dal Barco maps Lucy's arc in the Amazon series onto Plato's cave stage by stage: Vault 33's fake sky, curated history lessons, and Vault-Tec-managed information are the shadow-puppet show, her first step into the sun after Hank's abduction by Moldaver is the freed prisoner's blinding ascent, the hidden hospital vault tempts her (and Maximus, who wants to stay) like the return to the cave, and the truth - her father helped orchestrate the nuclear war, her mother is now a ghoul - plays the role the sun and the Good play in the Republic. Plato's claim that only the educated philosopher who has seen beyond the cave should govern (Republic 496a, 519a-d) explains why Lucy, unlike the frightened Norm or the tempted Maximus, goes back out into the wastes: she is becoming the philosopher-ruler whose hard-won knowledge enables Moldaver to restore power to the surface and begin a civilization no longer built on shadows. The chapter answers its own question - yes, it was worth leaving the vault for the truth.

samples.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
samples.title: He’s Got to Make His Own Mistakes
samples.relation: Cole pits Plato against Walter Benjamin to vindicate the imitation of Rush: Plato's cave makes art a shadow twice removed from the Forms, and on that view a perfect copy is impossible and every cover degraded, while Peart's 'Limelight' calls the stage a 'gilded cage' that is 'just a prettified cave' yet, with 'we are merely players' (via Shakespeare), makes performing the way out rather than deeper in. Benjamin's translator essay, with its 'language forest' echo and 'pure language', shows how Rush's cover of 'Summertime Blues' on Feedback layers Blue Cheer and the Who into one perception, and how live variations of 'Witch Hunt' and the premature chord of 'Turn the Page' let error overtake and become the new original. The chapter exceeds Aristotle's principle of non-contradiction in 'pure language', where original, copy, and fan covers (Rock Band failures, the South Park 'Lil' Rush' flub, Rick Mercer's drum lesson) are fragments of one greater vessel, so errors are portals of discovery.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Would You Help Me to Carry the Stone
samples.relation: Weinstein argues critics who call Waters a gloomy misanthrope misread him: he is an existentialist whose work maps point for point onto Camus's absurd, the human demand for unity endlessly frustrated. Waters's imagery tracks Camus's: the sun (Plato's cave symbol of the good, and the light Sisyphus loved on earth) against the eclipsed moon of death and madness; the stone we secrete through failed communication ('the bad blood slows and turns to stone' in 'Dogs,' 'would you help me to carry the stone' in The Wall) against Sisyphus's rock; and Pink's Trial, condemned for 'showing feelings of an almost human nature,' replaying Meursault's condemnation for failing to cry at his mother's funeral. Since the institutions of home, school, military, and the music industry's machine block every genuine encounter, Waters's persistence in making art that mostly fails to communicate is itself the absurd revolt, so with Camus one must imagine Sisyphus happy, and Weinstein imagines Waters happy too.

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 25 Fear of a Black Museum Black Existentialism
samples.relation: Charles Peterson reads the museum scene through Black existentialism and Africana phenomenology: colonial museums freeze African existence in an 'archaic amber' of aesthetic purity, and Killmonger's reclaiming of the mask and questioning of the curator perform a truth-telling that breaks the museum's performance of dominance. Du Bois's double-consciousness explains Killmonger's inseparable Wakandan-and-American two-ness (extended to Nakia and the War Dogs), while Paget Henry's contrast of the DuBoisian subject who oscillates between two 'We's' with Hegel's recognition-seeking subject explains why T'Chaka chooses Wakanda and abandons N'Jobu, and Plato's cave frames Killmonger as dragging Wakanda's comfortable council toward truths 'some truths are too much to bear.' The chapter concludes that Killmonger fails because wearing the mask he embraced negrification rather than shedding it, whereas T'Challa matures from a Hegelian into a DuBoisian subject by opening Wakanda to the world.

samples.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
samples.title: Conquering the Inner Demon
samples.relation: James Lawler casts Buffy as a contemporary allegory of Plato's cave-escaped philosopher and reads the show through Kant: the Slayer moves between a hellish lower world of instrumental appetite and an intelligible higher world of the soul, and Kant's Copernican revolution ('objects must conform to our knowledge') explains Marcie's invisibility in 'Out of Mind, Out of Sight' and the fear-made-flesh Master of 'Nightmares.' Kant's formula that every rational being exists as an end in himself grounds Buffy's duty in 'Anne' ('I am Buffy, the Vampire Slayer'), her rejection of Spike's chip as no substitute for a soul in 'Crush,' and her 'As You Were' admission that using Spike treats him as a mere means. Season Six explores 'too much heaven': Buffy's blissful death in 'The Gift' makes earthly life hell, and only conquering the inner demon — Willow's fear-driven dark magic defeated by Xander's yellow-crayon love in 'Grave' — restores the balance between heavens and hells.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: The Good Gossip
samples.relation: Borge weighs Jimmy Sirrel's claim that the best team always wins and the rest is gossip against Alex Ferguson insisting his side played better in a 1–4 defeat to Liverpool, framing the dispute as football Nominalism (only particular matches and results exist) versus football Platonism (an ideal way of playing exists over and above results). He rejects the Platonic ideal as metaphysically impossible—two perfect teams could never both score on every chance while conceding nothing, and style comparisons like catenaccio versus Brazil 1970 collapse without appeal to results—and instead uses possible-worlds counterfactuals: a team can be 'really' best yet unlucky when it creates objective scoring opportunities, like John Terry's slipped 2008 Champions League penalty or Spain's wrongly disallowed golden goal against South Korea in 2002, that go in across the closest possible worlds. Since Liverpool's deeply unfair 2005 comeback in Istanbul is celebrated as a classic, football is fiction and drama rather than a fairness-measuring contest, and the resulting what-if moaning is the good gossip that makes barstool debate worthwhile.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Conscious Unity “There’s No Place Like Home”
samples.relation: McLachlan maps the whole story onto Schelling's romantic eschatology: gray Kansas is the Ungrund, the boring unconscious unity; the tornado (and Dorothy Gale as 'the gale') is the alienating rupture; and 'there's no place like home' is conscious unity regained through love of concrete, limiting others—richer than the unity she left because it now contains real relationships. Each companion's quest begins in egoism (the Scarecrow as an almost perfect Platonist, all disembodied contemplation like the spider-watching Spinoza; the Tin Man's self-loving imperviousness to pain), while evil in Oz—Miss Gulch's totalizing order, the Witches' slave states, the hidden Wizard—is Schelling's second evil: the attempt to control everything and abolish the freedom of others. Against escape-eschatologies (Plato's shadow-world, Bunyan's Pilgrim who flees his family crying 'eternal life,' Dante turning from Beatrice to the divine light), the Schellingian lesson is that even God becomes personal through relation—which is why the Dainty China Princess's refusal to be a mantel ornament marks the exact point of Dorothy's education in love.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Reads South Park's music through the Greek doctrine of ethos: Sextus Empiricus' story of Pythagoras sobering drunk youths with slow aulos tunes and Plato's banishment of the soft Ionian and Lydian modes anticipate episodes where music directly changes behavior — Slayer's 'Raining Blood' scattering the hippie horde in 'Die Hippie Die', Cher blasted at the ATF standoff, and the Brown Noise in 'World Wide Recorder Concert'. Plato's tripartite soul maps how the Succubus's 'Morning After' spell enchants Chef's appetitive soul until the boys reverse the melody, while the Sirens' cosmic harmony in the Republic's Myth of Er links back to pitch-planet correspondences. Against Plato's view of music as inferior imitation, Schopenhauer's claim that music copies the Will itself explains why Grandpa's Enya torture in 'Death' communicates despair better than argument; authenticity judgments (Phil Collins appreciated only on Ritalin, Cartman's cynically reworded Faith + 1 hits) echo Plato's demand that music imitate the good.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: Of the Simple and Complex
samples.relation: The editors' introduction argues that Downton's quaint domestic plots burst with universal moral and social meaning beneath their surface. Using the season 1 snuffbox incident, in which Thomas frames the innocent Bates for theft, it shows how the episode stages archetypal villainy and innocence akin to the universal figures of Plato's Republic and world mythology, so the 'simple' plot is morally clear rather than superficial. It then reads the hierarchy of Thomas, Bates, and Lord Grantham through Confucian propriety and Aristotelian justice, suggesting that justice partly consists in attention to 'greater and lesser,' something Western viewers raised on equality find foreign yet intriguing. Finally it insists that as concrete persons all three are morally mixed (Thomas takes a beating to spare Jimmy, Bates may have killed outside the law, Grantham is generous to tenants but cold to his daughters), and that this complexity is what rewards philosophical reflection, along with Hume's 'small morals' of etiquette.

samples.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
samples.title: Smashing Critics’ Pumpkins
samples.relation: Reisch reconstructs the rock-critical case against Rush ('pretentious', 'ridiculous', Greg Kot's jibe that Peart drums 'like he's working out a calculus formula') as resting on an implicit Platonism: the Forms fix what a 'real' rock'n'roll band is, so a band mixing rock with philosophy, literature, and mathematical precision seems to violate the metaphysical grain of the universe rather than merely disappoint a taste. He explains the Forms through Plato's trees and the Form of the song ('La Villa Strangiato' and 'Happy Birthday'), reads Jack Black's 'one atom' praise of Peart as mathematics-as-highest-knowledge, and treats the 'Aristocrats' joke and UFO mocking Geddy Lee as incongruity humor at kinds illicitly combined. Dropping the Platonic metaphysics of kinds collapses the critics' syllogism into a bare insistence that different is bad, which is the revenge Gene Simmons ('What kind of band is Rush? It's Rush.') and Billy Corgan ('they just don't fit in a neat box') already delivered.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Tollefsen revives Plato's ancient quarrel between philosophy and poetry: artistic imitations, three removes from the Forms and aimed at the soul's emotional part, stir 'imitative emotions' - purer, shorter-lived, effort-free surrogates for the real labors of love, faith and community - and he builds a four-stage account of the U2 formula (idealized transcendent love in the lyrics, religious imagery fusing lover and God, the Edge's Big Music crescendo, and the concert 'you' extended to the crowd, as in the Elevation-tour 'I Will Follow' with its 'Amazing Grace' bells) to show U2 are masters of exactly this seduction. The healing fans felt after September 11th may therefore be an image of redemption rather than the reality. Where Aristotle and Aquinas would educate the emotions rather than suppress them, Tollefsen's quarrel is with imitation itself; his verdict is that U2 suffer from Misplaced Artistic Pretension - high imagery where honest trash (or genuine complexity) would do.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Pink Floyd From Pompeii to Philosophy
samples.relation: George Reisch's introduction reads the 1971 Live at Pompeii film, with the band playing to no audience inside a circular stone amphitheatre, as an ironic anticipation of The Wall, tracing how Waters's fury at stadium crowds (culminating in the 1977 Montreal spitting incident that spawned the wall concept) had not yet arrived. It frames the band's post-Barrett move from psychedelic whimsy to minimal formalism as philosophical stripping-away: Barrett wrote like an Aristotle fascinated by odd particulars ('Lucifer Sam,' 'The Gnome'), whose puzzlement at his impenetrable cat prefigures Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' and the problem of other minds, while Waters pursued Plato's monolithic 'forms' of time, money, and madness. On this reading Dark Side's closing 'the sun is eclipsed by the moon' indicts Being itself, making life essentially and permanently tragic, a circular trap signaled by The Wall's interlocking 'we came in?' and 'Isn't this where...'

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Rard tests whether objective morality survives the apocalypse by running four theories against Season Two: Plato's Forms explain universal truths about walkers ('walkers survive so long as their brains are relatively undamaged') but cannot handle white lies or changed circumstances, and Aristotle's virtue ethics reads Rick's rush from the shot Carl as rashness and Shane's supply run as courage, yet virtues prove relative and luck-dependent in a collapsed world. Natural law founders on clashing intuitions — Merle's racism and Hershel's barn of walkers each claim self-evidence. The chapter's center is Nietzschean: Hershel's barn is slave morality that pities the 'sick,' Maggie breaks from it, and Shane's sacrifice of Otis and opening of the barn enact a will-to-power master morality without joy, while Rick alone moves toward amor fati — embracing the world as it is, refusing guilt over Lori's affair, and insisting the baby be born into the Walk Age.

name: Socratic Ignorance (knowing that you don't know)

samples.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: Barad maps fifth-century Athens onto contemporary America to cast Stewart as a Socratic reformer confronting modern sophists, advertisers, pundits and media figures who make weaker arguments appear stronger without caring about truth, exemplified by Ed Helms admitting network stories are pre-written from 'conventional wisdom' and Ann Coulter's conformity-peddling. She details the shared method: flattering the 'expert', feigned ignorance, and layer-by-layer questioning that traps targets like Rumsfeld ('It may not seem like much, but for this administration it's a huge policy shift') in contradiction, with Socratic irony doing the work of Stewart's awestruck deadpan and mute astonished reactions to Bush clips. Against Bill O'Reilly's 'stoned slacker' charge she cites the Annenberg finding that the show's young audience is better informed, and weighs Ken Tucker's 'monkey' question through the Crossfire 'I'm not going to be your monkey' exchange, concluding that, like Socrates facing trial and execution, Stewart uses irony as means and truth as end.

samples.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
samples.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Vannatta explains why Seinfeld reruns now fall flat through Klosterman's neologism 'unironically': since about 1991 irony has become the invisible background of American comedy, a pervasive detachment that David Foster Wallace named and that Jedediah Purdy's For Common Things attacks as the gap between phenomenon and essence. Against Purdy's ironist (Seinfeld's Jerry, mastered by irony, believing in nothing but his own interests), the chapter sets Kierkegaard's Socrates, whose 'infinite absolute negativity' and confessing ignorance serve a truth he cannot define, and asks whether Klosterman, probing the gap between Bono's rehearsed car-ride persona and his inner self, is master of irony or mastered by it. The answer places Chuck midway between the two jailed ironists, Socrates and the Seinfeld finale: like Socrates he knows his own ignorance and serves the undefined idea of self-understanding, but only through pop-culture resemblance (KISS where Jerry used Superman), unable to master irony any more than he can bite his own teeth.

samples.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
samples.title: Where Do We Go from Here
samples.relation: David Kyle Johnson argues that Colbert's gut-thinking persona (the Harriet Miers 'I know her heart' bit, 'that's my right' on the Panama Canal) satirizes a real and widespread vice, and he refutes the philosophies behind it. Individual and moral relativism collapse into self-contradiction and absurdity ('Lincoln was not assassinated' would be 'true for' someone; Hitler could not be condemned), while gut-justification is what Locke called 'enthusiasm' - a belief that is 'its own proof,' circular like the prophet whose revelation needs no burning bush. Following Jamie Whyte, he dismantles the 'right to my opinion' (running example: the friend who insists on a grassy-knoll shooter despite the melon-head evidence): there is no epistemic or moral right to undefended belief, and no right to intellectual comfort. Against this he holds up Socrates, wisest because he alone admitted ignorance, and insists philosophy and politics progress only through argument, so truthiness is never an acceptable substitute.

samples.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
samples.title: Futurama and Philosophy
samples.relation: Mills-Knutsen reads the Brain Spawn - floating brains whose pain at others' thoughts drives them to dumb life down and finally to hoard all knowledge in the Infosphere ('The Day the Earth Stood Stupid,' 'The Why of Fry') - as Futurama's funhouse mirror of the West's distrust of intellectuals, from Pandora and Eve to Frankenstein and comic-book evil geniuses. Fry, the delta-brainwave-lacking hero made stupid by doing 'the nasty in the pasty,' stabs the Big Brain with Bonfire of the Vanities and later banishes the Brains to another dimension, just as Athens executed Socrates. A close reading of Plato's Apology - Socrates's feigned ignorance exposing everyone else's, his demand of free meals in lieu of exile, and his prophecy of even more annoying successors - maps onto the Big Brain's snobbery and onto universities (Wernstrom's tenure scam in 'A Big Piece of Garbage,' Amy's doctorate in 'That Darn Katz!') as society's way of paying intellectuals to stay out of the way.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Abraham Schwab turns Ygritte's 'You know nothing, Jon Snow' into a theory of epistemic humility: Jon misreads wildling courtship norms, Sam's dragonglass shatters on wight Small Paul, Lord Mormont assumes Mance fights like a southern king and pays for it at the Fist of First Men, while Arya's accurate self-knowledge keeps her alive. Formalizing with justified true belief - Sam's lucky dagger thrust is not knowledge, and the Watch's warranted belief that the dead Othor was harmless justifies falsity - he uses Lysa's letter, which sent Ned to King's Landing on a lie, to ask what justification is: Descartes's absolute certainty is too strict, reliabilism vindicates testimony ('dark wings, dark words'), so that only Sansa need witness Ned's beheading for the Starks to know it, and between Melisandre's circular dogma about Azor Ahai and total skepticism, moderate skepticism best governs belief - a humility the south lacked about the Horn of Winter.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Chapter 32 - “The Exit Door Leads In”
samples.relation: Eric Beck reads 'The Exit Door Leads In' as a modernized Platonic dialogue: like Oedipus before the Sphinx, the average salesman Bob Bibleman wins mandatory university admission by answering a computerized waiter's riddle, staging the Delphic 'Know Thyself' against Plato's Gorgias ideal of self-mastery, while Plato's Socrates in Charmides disclaims healthy self-knowledge. When Bibleman's terminal spills classified engine schematics, he decides not on universal principle but on what he thinks the authorities want; his honest answer that he would have handed them over anyway gets him expelled for failing a test he could not read, a double bind showing self-knowledge is contingent and situational. Dick thus revises knowing oneself as negotiation of the state's expectations rather than discovery of an essence, though the ending - Bibleman paying the computer after deciding not to - leaves open that he may one day rebel and need re-education.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Kirby reads the 'Imaginationland' trilogy as a satire of post-9/11 America interpreted through Ulrich Beck's world risk society: the Pentagon generals, still thinking in Cold War categories like 'Project X' and Chinese imagination portals, embody Beck's denial response and end up voting to nuke Imaginationland, while Cartman's Rambo-style self-interest embodies the apathetic response. Socrates' practice of demanding definitions frames the chapter's question of what terrorism actually is (via Hoffman's five criteria), and Socratic ignorance about what one does not know is contrasted with the worse condition of not being able to know what you do not know. Kyle's courtroom speech that imaginary beings like Luke Skywalker and Santa are 'realer' than most real people, and Butters' creative power to imagine Santa back to life, point to Beck's cosmopolitan 'transformation': imagination and cross-border cooperation as the way out of risk panic.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: If Not on the Island of Ethical Subjectivism, Then Where
samples.relation: George Wrisley uses Lost as a testing ground against ethical subjectivism and cultural relativism: the disagreement over Sayid shooting young Ben (monster or innocent child?) motivates relativism, but the Argument from Disagreement fails for the same reason Locke and Mr. Eko's button dispute does not change what will actually happen if it goes unpushed. Simple subjectivism makes every judge infallible (the Man in Black could declare his murders right) and dissolves genuine disagreement between Jacob and his brother over killing their 'mother,' while cultural relativism makes the Dharma Initiative's torture of Sayid 'right' and would have ruled Martin Luther King Jr. wrong. He concludes that Lost's ambiguous cases - Michael's murder of Ana Lucia and Libby, Ben killing Jacob, Jack extorting Ben on the operating table - invite viewers to seek objective grounds Socratically, questioning their own moral judgments with further 'why's.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: APPENDIX - Who are Locke, Hume, and Rousseau The Losties’ Guide to Philosophers
samples.relation: Scott Parker's appendix profiles the philosophers behind Lost's namesake characters: John Locke for the survivor (blank-slate empiricism, belief tempered by tolerance, The Reasonableness of Christianity), David Hume for Desmond (causation as habitual inference, with the button press as the image of induction, plus bundle-theory skepticism about the self), and Jean-Jacques Rousseau for Danielle ('man is naturally good, and only by institutions is he made bad,' private property as the root of inequality). It adds Jeremy Bentham (the alias on Locke's coffin), Kierkegaard via the Fear and Trembling Hurley finds under the Temple (Abraham's teleological suspension of the ethical and the leap of faith), Dogen on zazen, Edward Said for Sayid (Orientalism and the audience's own projected savagery onto the Others), and short lives of Kate Cooper Austin, Carlyle, Rutherford, Hugo Grotius, Bakunin, Ram Dass, Edmund Burke, Hawking, Minkowski, Faraday, C. S. Lewis, and Lennon.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 12. Why Blood Sacrifice
samples.relation: Philip Wilson defines sacrifice as gift-giving with payback ('I give x in order to get y') and reads Thanos's murder of Gamora through Agamemnon's sacrifice of Iphigenia at Aulis, while Black Widow's willing leap from the same cliff parallels Christ's atoning self-sacrifice. The core is Kierkegaard's Fear and Trembling: Abraham's binding of Isaac as the 'teleological suspension of the ethical,' where obeying God suspends universal morality, sharpened by Kant's argument that Abraham should have told the supposed divine voice he could never be certain it came from God. Wilson argues the films restore rather than suspend ethics, Gamora was murdered rather than sacrificed, Natasha died willingly with no collateral harm, and Tony's final 'I am Iron Man' self-sacrifice completes the tragic arc, leaving readers with Kierkegaard's sleepless questions about a moral order that demands blood.

samples.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
samples.title: Justified and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter reads preacher Billy St. Cyr's snake-handling through Kierkegaard's Fear and Trembling: like Abraham, Billy performs the absurd double movement - fully resigning himself to dying by rattlesnake while believing he will be spared - which is why Boyd Crowder, who abandoned faith for Hegel's objective rational certainty, can neither buy him out nor understand him. Kierkegaard's teleological suspension of the ethical explains why Billy and Abraham may set obedience to God above self-preservation and social morality, while Boyd's showdown in 'Truth and Consequences', where he hands Billy an un-milked rattlesnake, exposes that Billy's certainty has curdled into the hubris de Silentio warns against, so Billy is no Abraham. De Silentio's three marks - love, humility, no desire to instruct others - separate genuine faith from cult leaders and violent extremists.

samples.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Round argues modern zombie fiction's real horror is humanity, reading The Walking Dead existentially: Rick builds meaning through self-imposed missions, revises his morals ('You kill, you die' then killing Dexter anyway), and demands in his 'We ARE the walking dead' speech (Issue #24) that the group admit their new nature instead of hiding in bad faith behind old rules. Kierkegaard's Abraham illuminates Rick's suspension of universal ethics, while Sergeant Abraham Ford's confession 'No. I did what I wanted to do' models owning one's choices, and his angst after Eugene's lie shows the cost of projected meaning collapsing. Camus supplies persistence against the absurd (suicides like Jim, Jacqui, and Carol exert the only control left), and Adorno's Marxist critique frames the Governor's Woodbury as an inauthentic hierarchy that denies its people authentic choice.

samples.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
samples.title: 15 Indiana Jones and the Leap of Faith
samples.relation: Uses Kierkegaard's Fear and Trembling to argue that Indy's step off the lion's head in Last Crusade is not a genuine leap of faith: Abraham's leap rests on absurd trust in God and the 'teleological suspension of the ethical,' whereas Indy acts to save his father and risks arming the Nazis — making him at most a tragic hero choosing between competing ethical duties. The chapter then sorts the film's believers into Kierkegaard's two knights, classifying Kazim of the Brotherhood as a Knight of Infinite Resignation, the Grail Knight as a near-miss Knight of Faith (he guards rather than lives in the ordinary world), and Henry and Marcus as devout but neither. Kierkegaard would complain that modern faith is 'dirt cheap' compared with Abraham's arduous biblical faith, and Indy's relief at not falling confirms he is no Knight of Faith.

samples.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
samples.title: 21. Stannis—Knight of Faith or Tragic Hero
samples.relation: Devlin asks whether Stannis, who burns Shireen to save his army, is Kierkegaard's knight of faith or merely a tragic hero. Stannis's duty-obsessed deontology - knighting Davos while cutting off his fingertips, striking 'beloved brother' from a letter as a lie - is Kantian, and the Shireen dilemma looks like Abraham's teleological suspension of the ethical; yet because Stannis always calculates and justifies ('Faith? In a real war, the side with the greater number wins nine times out of ten'), he never makes the leap on the strength of the absurd, and Davos ends up following Kant's own verdict on Abraham: 'If he commands you to burn children, your lord is evil.' He is therefore a tragic hero in the line of Agamemnon and Jephthah, rationally comprehensible and fittingly undone by Brienne's 'do your duty.'

samples.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
samples.title: 16. Gotta Have Faith
samples.relation: Winters asks what faith is when the Party risks burning and becoming demodog chow so Eleven can close the gate: after arguing via George Michael and the talisman-free tunnels that faith need not be religious, he tests Bishop's models of faith against 'The Gate' (the affective and secular hope models fit; the belief and trust models fail because everyone has seen the Mind Flayer's work on Will). Hume's account that causation is never observed, only habituated, explains the Party's hope that heat will drive the Mind Flayer from Will and that Christmas lights will reach him, and Kierkegaard's teleological suspension of the ethical and knight of faith frame Eleven's willingness to die against the absurd, since aligning her life with friendship's higher purpose is what makes it meaningful.

samples.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
samples.title: Kierkegaard Lays It Down
samples.relation: Willie Young uses the sacrifice bunt (Derek Jeter's perfect one versus Placido Polanco's failed one) to test philosophical accounts of sacrifice. Aristotle treats bunting for teammates as friendship and civic virtue in the polis, while Seneca's Stoic sacrifices only to exercise virtue itself, detached from particular friends and refusing retaliation for hit batters. Hegel's modern ideal of self-renunciation makes the player a cog in the team machine (the Big Red Machine), obeying the manager's calculations; against this, Kierkegaard's Abraham, whose absolute duty to God is 'higher than the universal' through infinite resignation, exposes baseball's mechanical, manager-ordered sacrifice and asks whether the game trains obedient citizens who sacrifice as they are told.

samples.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This file spans book chapters 4-11. Elizabeth Losh reads Facebook games (Zombies, Mob Wars, Scrabulous, Parking Wars, PackRat, (Lil) Green Patch) through Goffman's 'face', Brown and Levinson's politeness, and Derrida's gift-obligation, showing that aggressive games can be played politely while altruistic ones coerce; Jeremy Sarachan analyzes profile pictures through Barthes's studium, punctum and 'air' and Benjamin's mechanical reproduction (the webcam image that has no original). Mimi Marinucci pairs Glaucon's Ring of Gyges with Suler's online disinhibition effect to argue that Facebook's forced integration of audiences (students, colleagues, Mom all reading one profile) suppresses 'fronting' and so can foster authentic self-expression; Mariam Thalos answers with Sartre's analysis of the gaze and Beauvoir's woman-as-Other that the elective, endlessly plastic profile cannot anchor the bonding only face-to-face encounter provides - hence 'Why I Am Not a Friend' - while Wandel and Beavers use Groundhog Day's Phil Connors and Goffman's presentation of self to defend identity play as real self-discovery, and Vejby and Wittkower ask whether Facebook is Debord's Spectacle 2.0 or a platform for Situationist detournement. Finally, Craig Condella measures 'friending' against Aristotle's three friendships and Cicero's 'handmaid of virtue' (via the Seinfeld episode where Keith Hernandez asks Jerry to help him move), and Matthew Tedesco sets 322 Facebook friends against Godwin's burning archbishop to press the utilitarian impartiality challenge, deploying Williams's 'one thought too many' shipwreck case and criticizing Frank Jackson's sector-plan defense of partiality.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 11. Louis C.K.’s No-Bullshit Philosophy
samples.relation: Marie Snyder uses Sartre's existentialism to unpack Louis's Conan monologue about the 'forever empty': with God gone we are condemned to be free, thrown into a world with no ready-made purpose and alone with our choices - which explains both the cellphone distraction economy and the Live in Portland bit that 'even if you're with someone, you're alone.' Authenticity means ruthlessly honest self-awareness and owning every choice with no excuses - Sartre's waiter example, the claim that there is no cowardly temperament, and Louis's refusal to let 'a flaw in the human male' excuse the tits bit or porn masturbation. Since in choosing for ourselves we choose for all humanity, Snyder pairs Sartre's universalized responsibility with Louis's 'act in a way that, if everybody acted that way, things would work out,' and reads intimate others, as in the Sartre-Beauvoir open relationship, as mirrors that reflect us back to ourselves against the connectionless 'we're just cummers' porn culture. Bad faith - self-deception, distraction, blame - is the fallenness Louis keeps diagnosing in his audiences and confessing in himself.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Rise and Shine It’s On Again Off Again
samples.relation: Surber proposes Kristeva's 'abject aesthetics' as the new pair of shades that makes Radiohead legible: 'Creep' expresses abjection (the creep excluded even from recognition by the beautiful people), the android of 'Paranoid Android' is a borderline phenomenon neither human nor machine, and the bodily imagery of 'Bones', 'My Iron Lung', and the corpse in 'Knives Out' enacts the eruption of the pre-linguistic, formless abject, as do Donwood's dissolving Kid A letters. He contrasts the Beatles' aesthetics of psychedelic transcendence and Pink Floyd's existentialist aesthetics of alienation — built on Sartre's 'Hell is other people' gaze and the being-for-itself/being-in-itself split — with Radiohead's fluid, boundary-less world where meanings never come into focus and no existential revolt is possible because the embodied self is part of the world. Against the charge of nihilism, he reads Hail to the Thief and In Rainbows ('How come I end up where I started?') as postmodern reconstruction: if boundaries and meanings are fluid, they can also be remade.

samples.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
samples.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
samples.relation: Reads Larry as a textbook existentialist: his agonizing over trivia ('Doctor?... Pharmacist?') instantiates Heideggerian anxiety and Sartrean anguish, because every choice, even yanking his 5 wood out of a casket in 'The 5 Wood,' proclaims an image of how everyone ought to live. Since existence precedes essence there is no fixed human nature for Larry to appeal to; he must author his values alone, which the chapter says also makes him an optimist ('I'm not an inventor, but I'm an improver'). Larry dispels others' bad faith when he tells Susie she obviously can share the brownie recipe in 'The Benadryl Brownie,' and his baldness crusade, firing the toupee-wearing chef Phil Dunlap in 'The Grand Opening,' is a demand for authenticity about one's facticity. The 'Larry David Stare' is analyzed through Sartre's Look: the squinter tries to inspect another consciousness empirically and necessarily fails, since the other's freedom can never be objectified.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 9. Another Wig Underneath
samples.relation: Cooper argues that the 'vulnerability' Drag Race demands is really a marketable persona, not truth. Working through Butler's Gender Trouble (built on Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes a woman'), she concedes drag reveals gender's imitative structure, but shows it also confirms identity: Latrice Royale's padded 'Natural Woman' lip sync reads as authentic, and trans queens like Peppermint and Gia Gunn use drag to articulate womanhood, with Husserl's intersubjectivity invoked to insist that constructed gender is no less real for not being empirical. Willam's edit-spliced 'I'm not acting' breakdown and Shannel's deliberate wig-doff show honesty becoming inconsequential next to spectacle, while Untucked's Interior Illusions Lounge is framed as Sartre's No Exit hell of unending observation. Against RuPaul's 'born naked' self-help nihilism ('identity is a joke'), she ends warning that the show no longer lets Katya take off the chicken suit.

samples.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
samples.title: 4. Faces from Another Dimension
samples.relation: Hooke frames the volume through Levinas's claim that the face presents itself from a dimension of transcendence, with Kierkegaard's Abraham, Sartre's existential look, and Beauvoir's faces of the elderly and the second sex in the background, plus Lingis on trust. He shows how TZ masks its deadliest figures with trusted faces — Robert Redford as Death in 'Nothing in the Dark,' Sebastian Cabot's avuncular Pip revealing 'This is the other place!' in 'A Nice Place to Visit,' the witch of 'Jess-Belle,' the gentle Kanamits whose book turns out to be a cookbook — so that proof of trust is nearly impossible and the show has us laughing with the Devil. The Turing test is applied to Alicia's tear in 'The Lonely' (clearly in love 'regardless of the organs or hardware beneath'), the slot machine of 'The Fever,' and the aged couple of 'The Trade-Ins,' whose faces silently recognize a lost shared life.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Applies Sartre's Being and Nothingness to the mockumentary: Pam's bad faith consists in pretending she has no choice between Jim and Roy (her garbled 'I'm not into Jim' conversation with Karen in 'Ben Franklin'), while the camera's Look - Sartre's keyhole peeper caught in the hallway - turns her into an object not of her making when she is caught watching Jim and Karen in 'The Merger', and her shame finally lets her own her feelings. David Brent's pride (posing with his Inside Paper magazine cover) tries to control the Other's look and fails, since the freely respected gaze he craves cannot be extracted; and the ever-possible camera functions as Foucault's panopticon (Bentham's prison design), visible and unverifiable, silencing Jan on speakerphone in 'Cocktails' and forcing Dwight and Angela's 'Don't linger. Break left' choreography, which makes the viewer a complicit co-worker.

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: What Do We Hear when We Listen to Our iPods
samples.relation: Wittkower opens with his cat Wallace at the window to show hearing is selective, then applies Sartre's account of the Look -- the voyeur at the keyhole hearing a footstep, the other as a 'void within being' -- to ask when sounds announce another person, the iPod-era rustle becoming the sudden 'appearance of a face.' Drawing on Marx's early claim that our senses are socially estranged, so that we meet others only as waiters, clerks, and price tags ('we are not our khakis'), he argues the audio cocoon both limits and enables encounter: mostly we hear our own identity reflected back ('I am the kind of person who listens to Amy Winehouse'). The governing image is Odysseus lashed to the mast, hearing the Sirens without being able to act, and the chapter closes by rehabilitating Marx as the first philosopher of technology alongside Heidegger, Dewey, Lukacs, Adorno, and Habermas.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: The End
samples.relation: Hiu M. Chan contrasts Zhuangzi's butterfly dream with Inception's plot: Zhuangzi forgets his self, dreams without planning, and ends in the 'transformation and unity' of dreamer and butterfly, whereas Cobb's self is constantly highlighted — he plans missions, codes his dreams with motifs (the spinning top, the dream machine, the faceless children, distinct locations, weather, crosscutting), and can never fuse dream and reality. The chapter maps the film's four-layer 'meta-space' narrative structure (exposition through resolution distributed across dream layers) and argues the 'dreams' are really programmed, coded narrative devices, the opposite of the Daoist 'whole' in which reality itself is the biggest dream and a true person no longer dreams. Against semiotic 'dream explaining' (the top means dreaming), she holds that in Daoism the top would mean nothing beyond a spinning top, and contrasts Nolan with Tarkovsky's 'dream worshipping' films like The Mirror. The ending's reunion is thus only apparent: Inception lacks the Daoist harmony that would let Cobb 'become the butterfly.'

samples.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Bein reads the LEGO brick as the Daodejing's 'uncarved block': a single brick is an invitation rather than a toy, and precisely because it is empty of meaning (and mostly empty of plastic — the stud-and-tube marriage of yin and yang) it can become anything, whereas printed, specialized pieces 'are diminished by being added to'. Against the Greek obsession with definition — Socrates refusing sophistry while insisting one cannot rule justly without defining justice, Plato's definition dialogues, Aristotle's inheritance of the precision ideal, and William James's 'think clearly' — Daoist imprecision is defended as a philosophical stance: dao is a way, an activity, not a thing. Wei wu wei ('doing without doing') explains Emmet's winning plan of building the utterly ordinary Octan spaceship, why Lord Business's penny-throw is genius without sagacity (coercive, not water-like), and why governing should be like cooking a small fish — minimal, attentive intervention.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: I Still Miss Someone The Self and Its Travels Along the Way
samples.relation: Geisz explains the Confucian social dao of ritual (li), humaneness (ren), filial piety and the junzi, the Daodejing's metaphysical Dao with its unity of opposites, and Zhuangzi's tales of free wandering, then maps all three onto Cash's songs. Zhuangzi's "Free and Easy Wandering" answers Cash's road songs ("I've Been Everywhere," "The Wanderer"), Cook Ding's effortless carving answers John Henry's hammering in "The Legend of John Henry's Hammer," and the scrambled countdown of "Twenty-Five Minutes to Go" echoes Zhuangzi's logic-bending humor. The payoff is Cash's own country Yin-Yang of interdependent opposites, freedom chained to imprisonment ("Folsom Prison Blues"), sin twinned with redemption ("I Hung My Head"), fidelity with betrayal ("Jackson," "Cocaine Blues"), and a self that, unlike Zhuangzi's self-forgetting sage, must travel a temporal path carrying its guilt, yet stays on what Geisz calls a very wide superhighway of a Dao.

samples.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
samples.title: The Way of the Archer
samples.relation: White reads Clint Barton through the Tao Te Ching and Chuang Tzu: Hawkeye's instinctive archery—'use your bow gently, naturally, instinctively'—is wei wu wei, while his bragging, his glory-chasing failure against Iron Man, and his attempt to become Goliath all violate it by striving against his own nature, until the Kree-Skrull War teaches him the bow is his way.
